A1.justification: Despite the changed title and expanded authorship, both PDFs describe the same spurious-correlation survey. All 11 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3 support comparison of text, equations, tables, figures, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reviews published research. Table 1 catalogs existing datasets, and Figure 2 illustrates chest X-ray artifacts; neither reports original experimental or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains a literature survey. Its expanded application discussions and illustrations summarize cited studies or explain possible failures, without reporting original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes its own algorithm or model. v3 expands and recategorizes surveyed methods, but this does not establish a change to an algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure produced by this work.

E1.justification: Table 1 expands the reviewed dataset catalog, including graph and additional multimodal benchmarks, while removing Spawrious. Neither survey actually uses these datasets for training or evaluation, so executed dataset and task coverage remains absent.

E2.justification: Both versions discuss methods such as ERM, Group DRO, and JTT as prior research. Neither evaluates a comparator set against a proposed method; additional method citations in v3 are literature-review additions.

E3.justification: The documented accuracy computations are corrected: v2 Section 4.2 uses indicators of incorrect predictions, whereas v3 Section 5.2 uses correct predictions for the same three accuracy metrics. This revises the reported metric formulas without establishing any changed or rerun experiment.

E4.justification: No new ablation, sensitivity sweep, or separately reported robustness analysis is conducted. The added reward-model and ProcTHOR figures are explanatory examples, and the application discussions synthesize cited research rather than present new case-study experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for empirical results produced by the survey.

E6.justification: v3 adds specific qualitative findings from cited studies, including late-training degradation under some group-balancing schemes and benefits of combining balancing approaches (Section 4.1.2), plus task-dependent strengths of fine-tuning methods (Section 4.3.2). These are newly reported literature findings, not original experiments or matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds a core/spurious input decomposition and a heuristic representation-alignment relation in Equation 3. It also corrects the accuracy indicators in v2 Equations 3–5. Definition 2.1 and the ERM and worst-group risk objectives remain substantively unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a survey providing a definition, method taxonomy, dataset catalog, metrics, and research directions. v3 explicitly adds broader impacts to its advertised scope, developed through LLM alignment, healthcare, and embodied AI; it introduces no new algorithmic or performance claim.

C2.justification: Sections 2.3 and 6 add substantial explanations of persistent spurious representations, regularization failure, reward-model biases, clinical shortcuts, and embodied-agent failures. Section 7 expands limitations concerning validation without group labels, interpretability, scalability, and cross-modal generalization, while retaining the earlier robustness–utility tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 Table 1 adds dataset access hyperlinks, source-paper references, attribute counts, and synthetic/natural labels. It revises metadata, including CivilComments' class count from 7 to 2. Section 5.1 adds construction and curation explanations; these are documentation improvements, not disclosed changes to experimental runs.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands the reviewed literature across theoretical feature learning, data balancing, graph methods, LLM alignment, healthcare, and robotics. Related research areas receive much fuller treatment. Spawrious and its Lynch et al. reference are removed, while many existing methods are retained under reorganized categories.

P1.justification: Existing explanations are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Related Areas becomes a standalone section, method categories and subsection ordering change, Broader Impacts becomes a dedicated section, and the conclusion becomes Final Remarks within Discussion. The title and author block also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Table 1 expands from 21 to 45 datasets and from five to eight columns. The taxonomy is substantially redrawn, the chest X-ray figure is relocated, and four illustrations are added: Clever Hans, correlation shift, sycophancy, and ProcTHOR scenes.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects erroneous accuracy formulas and provides a more useful reference through sourced dataset links, construction explanations, and more specific discussions of mechanisms and limitations. These gains are partly offset by a new taxonomy inconsistency: Section 4.3 classifies Group DRO under methods for already trained models, although its own description identifies a training-objective method. The net improvement is positive but qualified.
